title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of vitamin D and urinary tract infection
author: Niwanda Yogiswara
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be2tjgen

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Search multiple databases including MEDLINE, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov using MeSH terms for 'vitamin D deficiency', 'vitamin D', 'Vitamin D supplementation', 'urinary tract infection', 'cystitis', and 'pyelonephritis'.

substeps.instruction: Search the full reference lists of included studies.
Manage references using data management software.
Apply no date or language restrictions.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Execute a three-stage selection process to identify eligible observational studies (prospective/retrospective cohorts, case-control, cross-sectional, nested case-control) and interventional studies (non-randomized control trials, RCTs, crossover trials).

substeps.instruction: Screen titles and abstracts of all electronic papers using Mendeley reference manager software to assess potential eligibility.
Retrieve full-texts for all articles presumed to meet criteria.
Exclude case-reports, small case series (<10 patients), letters to the editor, conference proceedings, animal studies, and review articles.

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Two authors must independently extract data from the selected studies, resolving any discrepancies through consensus of all authors.

substeps.instruction: Extract the following parameters: name of first author, year of publication, study design, number of participants, location of the study, participant's age, level of 25(OH)D, and OR of UTI.

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality of included studies independently by two authors, resolving disagreements through consensus.

substeps.instruction: Use the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) for case-control studies (evaluating patient selection, comparability of cases and controls, ascertainment of exposure, and non-response rate).
Use the NOS for cohort studies (evaluating selection, comparability of exposed/non-exposed cohorts, assessment of outcome, and adequacy of follow-up period).
Use Cochrane risk of bias assessment tools for RCTs (evaluating random sequence generation, allocation concealment, selective reporting, and participant and personnel).

steps.title: Synthesize and Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Perform a qualitative synthesis to account for high inter-study heterogeneity.

substeps.instruction: Use odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (95% CI) for binary outcomes.
Use mean difference (MD) and 95% CI for continuous outcomes.
If p < 0.1 and I² > 50%, utilize the random-effect DerSimonian model.
Perform subgroup analysis based on study age group, gender, location, study design, and cut-off definition of vitamin D deficiency.
